name: WATER
aliases: Waterjet Ablation Therapy for Endoscopic Resection of prostate tissue
question: Is robotic waterjet resection (Aquablation) noninferior to TURP for relieving BPH symptoms in men with 30 to 80 mL prostates?

design.population: Men aged 45 to 80 years with moderate-to-severe BPH-related LUTS (IPSS 12 or higher, Qmax below 15 mL/s) and a 30 to 80 mL prostate on transrectal ultrasound; 181 were treated.
design.locator: 5-year report (Can J Urol 2022) pp10961-10963, Figure 1; arm sizes of 117 and 67 from 3-year report (Can J Urol 2020) Table 1

verdictNote: Symptom relief noninferior at 6 months; primary safety endpoint favored Aquablation (26% versus 42%).
takeaway: Aquablation, an image-guided robotic waterjet resection, was compared with TURP in men with 30 to 80 mL prostates: it was noninferior for 6-month IPSS reduction and had fewer persistent grade 1 or grade 2 or higher complications at 3 months (26% versus 42%).

reports.label: Primary report (6-month efficacy, 3-month safety)
reports.citation: Gilling P, Barber N, Bidair M, et al. "WATER: A Double-Blind, Randomized, Controlled Trial of Aquablation® vs Transurethral Resection of the Prostate in Benign Prostatic Hyperplasia." *J Urol.* 2018;199(5):1252-1261. doi:10.1016/j.juro.2017.12.065
reports.followUp: 6 months for the IPSS endpoint; 3 months for the primary safety endpoint

results.measure: Mean IPSS reduction from baseline at 6 months (Aquablation minus TURP)
results.note: Noninferiority margin 4.7 IPSS points; superiority not reached (p=0.1347). The difference is 1.8 points in favor of Aquablation.
results.locator: Abstract (noninferiority p<0.0001); means, mean difference 1.8, margin and superiority p=0.1347 in the primary report (J Urol 2018) Methods and Results; the 5-year report (Can J Urol 2022) restates the means and difference and gives superiority p=.1346; CI from FDA De Novo summary DEN170024 p12

results.measure: Clavien-Dindo persistent grade 1 or grade 2 or higher procedure-related complications at 3 months
results.note: Noninferiority met (margin 10 percentage points), then superiority tested and met (p=0.0149). Difference is Aquablation minus TURP in percentage points.
results.locator: Abstract; difference by subtraction (the Plante 2019 abstract gives the same 26% versus 42%); noninferiority margin of 10 percentage points from the 5-year report (Can J Urol 2022) p10962 and the FDA De Novo summary DEN170024

results.measure: Anejaculation among sexually active men
results.note: Sexually active men without anejaculation at baseline.

harms.label: Persistent grade 1 events at 3 months
harms.locator: 5-year report (Can J Urol 2022) p10964; restates the 3-month primary safety data

harms.label: Grade 2 or higher events at 3 months
harms.locator: 5-year report (Can J Urol 2022) p10964; restates the 3-month primary safety data

harms.label: Blood transfusion
harms.locator: 5-year report (Can J Urol 2022) p10964 and Figure 1
harms.note: Denominators are the treated groups in the CONSORT diagram. No late bleeding event required transfusion in either arm.

harms.label: De novo erectile dysfunction or incontinence requiring a pad

delivery.label: Hospital length of stay
delivery.note: Urinary catheter removed a median of 1 day after surgery in both groups.

delivery.label: Hemostasis after Aquablation
delivery.value: Focal non-resective electrocautery or low-pressure Foley balloon inflation in the prostatic fossa; continuous bladder irrigation in all patients.

reports.label: Subgroup analysis (prostate size, middle lobe, severity)
reports.citation: Plante M, Gilling P, Barber N, et al. "Symptom relief and anejaculation after aquablation or transurethral resection of the prostate: subgroup analysis from a blinded randomized trial." *BJU Int.* 2019;123(4):651-660. doi:10.1111/bju.14426
reports.followUp: 6 months for IPSS; 3 months for the primary safety endpoint

results.measure: IPSS reduction at 6 months, men with prostates 50 to 80 g (difference, Aquablation minus TURP)
results.note: Four points greater after Aquablation than after TURP, versus 1.8 points overall (p=0.135). Prespecified and post hoc exploratory subgroup analyses.

results.measure: Persistent grade 1 or grade 2 or higher complications, men with prostates 50 to 80 g
results.note: 26-point difference; overall result 26% versus 42% (p=0.015).

results.measure: Anejaculation among sexually active men with prostates 50 to 80 g
results.note: Overall result 10% versus 36%.

results.measure: IPSS change by baseline anatomy
results.note: Exploratory analysis showed larger IPSS changes after Aquablation in men with enlarged middle lobes, severe middle lobe obstruction, a low baseline maximum flow rate and a postvoid residual above 100 mL.

reports.label: One-year follow-up
reports.citation: Gilling PJ, Barber N, Bidair M, et al. "Randomized Controlled Trial of Aquablation versus Transurethral Resection of the Prostate in Benign Prostatic Hyperplasia: One-year Outcomes." *Urology.* 2019;125:169-173. doi:10.1016/j.urology.2018.12.002

results.measure: Mean IPSS reduction at 12 months
Mean improvement in maximum urinary flow rate at 12 months
Surgical retreatment for BPH within 1 year
results.note: Not significant.

delivery.label: Late procedure-related adverse events
delivery.value: No procedure-related adverse events after month 6.

reports.label: Two-year follow-up
reports.citation: Gilling P, Barber N, Bidair M, et al. "Two-Year Outcomes After Aquablation Compared to TURP: Efficacy and Ejaculatory Improvements Sustained." *Adv Ther.* 2019;36(6):1326-1336. doi:10.1007/s12325-019-00952-3
reports.followUp: 24 months; visit completed in 169 of 181 treated patients (93%)
reports.followUpLocator: Europe PMC full text PMC6824383, Results, first paragraph

results.measure: Mean IPSS reduction at 2 years
results.note: 95% CI for the difference -2.1 to 2.6 points as reported. At least 5 points of improvement in 89% (Aquablation) and 95% (TURP).

results.measure: Mean improvement in maximum urinary flow rate at 2 years
results.note: 95% CI for the difference -1.3 to 6.4 as reported.

results.measure: Cumulative surgical retreatment for BPH over 2 years
results.note: Between years 1 and 2, 2 Aquablation patients (1.7%) and none in the TURP group were retreated surgically (p=1).

harms.label: Urinary retention, months 12 to 24
harms.note: Rates of individual events between years 1 and 2 were low and similar across groups; adverse events after month 12 were not adjudicated by the clinical events committee.

harms.label: Stricture or adhesions, months 12 to 24
harms.note: No erectile dysfunction events in either arm.

delivery.label: Blinding at 2 years
delivery.note: p=0.0021; partly due to earlier protocol versions that blinded patients only through the primary endpoint.

reports.label: Three-year follow-up
reports.dateLocator: PubMed entry date; issue dated February 2020
reports.citation: Gilling P, Barber N, Bidair M, et al. "Three-year outcomes after Aquablation therapy compared to TURP: results from a blinded randomized trial." *Can J Urol.* 2020;27(1):10072-10079.
reports.noDoi: The Canadian Journal of Urology does not assign DOIs to these articles; PMID 32065861.
reports.followUp: 36 months; 97 of 116 Aquablation (84%) and 55 of 65 TURP (85%) patients had 3-year follow-up

results.measure: Mean IPSS reduction at 3 years
results.note: Reported difference 0.6 points (95% CI -3.3 to 2.2). In men with prostates of 50 cc or more, the reduction averaged 3.5 points larger after Aquablation across the 3 years (p=0.0125, repeated measures).

results.measure: Mean improvement in maximum urinary flow rate at 3 years
results.note: Reported difference 3.3 cc/s (95% CI -0.5 to 7.1).

results.measure: Cumulative surgical retreatment for BPH through 3 years
results.note: No surgical retreatment beyond 20 months in either arm.

harms.label: Serious adverse events between years 2 and 3
harms.note: Cardiac arrest, two myocardial infarctions and a small bowel obstruction after Aquablation, none related to the procedure; aspiration pneumonia with respiratory failure after TURP, unrelated to the procedure.

delivery.label: Medical therapy failure at 3 years
delivery.note: Alpha blocker or 5-alpha reductase inhibitor started after surgery.

reports.label: Five-year follow-up
reports.dateLocator: PubMed entry date; issue dated February 2022
reports.citation: Gilling PJ, Barber N, Bidair M, et al. "Five-year outcomes for Aquablation therapy compared to TURP: results from a double-blind, randomized trial in men with LUTS due to BPH." *Can J Urol.* 2022;29(1):10960-10968.
reports.noDoi: The Canadian Journal of Urology does not assign DOIs to these articles; PMID 35150215.
reports.followUp: 60 months; 58 of 116 Aquablation (50%) and 32 of 65 TURP (49%) patients

results.measure: Mean IPSS reduction at 5 years
results.note: Median IPSS at 5 years 5.5 (Aquablation) and 6 (TURP).

results.measure: IPSS reduction across all follow-up visits, men with prostates of 50 mL or more
results.note: Reduction was 3.5 points greater after Aquablation (repeated measures analysis); no difference in the age or baseline IPSS subgroups.

results.measure: Mean improvement in maximum urinary flow rate at 5 years
Mean reduction in postvoid residual at 5 years
Additional BPH medication or surgery for recurrent LUTS through 5 years
results.note: The report describes this as 51% less in the Aquablation arm. By the table, 6 Aquablation patients (2 TURP and 1 laser procedure in year 1, 2 TURP in year 2, 1 TURP in year 5) and 1 TURP patient had a surgical procedure.

harms.label: Persistent grade 1 events at 3 months
harms.note: Procedure-related anejaculation, p=0.0004. Urinary complications from 3 to 5 years did not differ between groups.

harms.label: Grade 2 or higher events at 3 months

delivery.label: MSHQ-EjD change over 5 years
delivery.value: Averaged 2.7 points lower (worse) after TURP across all visits (p=0.0015); close to 0 after Aquablation.

delivery.label: Erectile function (IIEF-5)
delivery.value: No statistically significant change in either group through 5 years.

reports.label: Five-year outcomes in 50 to 80 mL prostates
reports.dateLocator: PubMed entry date; issue dated October 2023
reports.citation: Oumedjbeur K, Corsi NJ, Bouhadana D, et al. "Aquablation versus TURP: 5-year outcomes of the WATER randomized clinical trial for prostate volumes 50-80 mL." *Can J Urol.* 2023;30(5):11650-11658.
reports.noDoi: The Canadian Journal of Urology does not assign DOIs to these articles; PMID 37838991.
reports.followUp: Up to 5 years; 62 Aquablation and 34 TURP patients with 50 to 80 mL prostates

results.measure: Mean IPSS reduction across 5 years of follow-up, 50 to 80 mL subgroup
results.note: Repeated measures analysis across visits; the Aquablation arm had slightly larger baseline prostates (66.4 versus 61.7 mL).

results.measure: Additional BPH medication or surgery through 5 years, 50 to 80 mL subgroup
results.note: Risk difference -14.4% (95% CI -2.29 to -30.4, as printed). Surgical reintervention 1.6% versus 3.1%; return to BPH medication 1.6% versus 15.6%.

results.measure: Persistent grade 1 ejaculatory dysfunction, 50 to 80 mL subgroup
results.note: Risk difference -21.9% (95% CI -32.5 to -10.7).

harms.label: Persistent grade 1 or grade 2 or higher events
harms.note: Risk difference -23.1% (95% CI -28.9 to -15.5). The abstract places this endpoint at 3 months and the Results text at 6 months.

harms.label: Grade 3a events
harms.note: Bleeding 1 versus 1; stricture or adhesions 1 versus 1.

harms.label: Grade 3b events
harms.note: Urinary retention 1 after Aquablation; bleeding 1 and stricture or adhesions 1 after TURP. No grade 4 events.

delivery.label: Hemostasis after Aquablation
delivery.value: Electrocautery in 24 patients and low-pressure Foley balloon inflation in 38.
